newsitem.title: USA: SatCon gets contract to develop alternator.
newsitem.headline: SatCon gets contract to develop alternator.

text.p: SatCon Technology Corp said Monday it received a $500,000 contract from the Department of Energy to develop a high-speed motor alternator for use in hybrid electric vehicles (HEV).
It said the alternator will have a peak power of 30 kilowatts and a speed of 30,000 revolutions per minute.
A SatCon spokeswoman said the company will be working with the Massachusetts Institute of Technology in the design and technical evaluation of the alternator.
The timetable for the project is 18 months, she added.
David Eisenhaure, president and chief executive of SatCon, said the program to develop high speed motor alternator is aimed at lowering the cost of HEVs.
He said the device his company will build will be used in the flywheel energy storage system of HEVs.
He said the project also supports SatCon's work in space-based flywheel and other terrestrial flywheel applications.
With appropriate scaling, the alternator could also be used in machine tools, he said.
He added that SatCon's new subsidiary, K&D Magmotor, will participate in designing the device to help reduce its cost and to establish a market potential for the devices once the design is complete.
